'''Aleksandra Kornhauser Frazer''' (26 September 1926{{spnd}}17 May 2020) was a [[Slovenia|Slovenian]] [[chemist]]. She was a Professor of Chemistry at the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Engineering and Director at the International Centre for Chemical Studies, of the [[University of Ljubljana]], Slovenia.<ref name="rtvslo1"/>

==Early life==
Born as '''Aleksandra Caleari'''<ref name="rtvslo1"/> into a wealthy family with five siblings—her father owned what would later become the Jelovica company in [[Škofja Loka]]. The family lost their wealth during the [[Great Depression]] in the 1930s and she grew up in relative poverty. In 1940 during World War II, at the age of fifteen, she began running a youth organization to support [[Partisan (military)|partisan]]s. Her father was imprisoned in the [[Concentration Camp|concentration camp]] in [[Begunje]] and the family were roped into forced labor but all survived the war. After briefly teaching in [[Kamnik]] and [[Domžale]], she went to university in to study [[chemistry]] and graduated in 1963.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.delo.si/nedelo/zame-je-vsak-dan-srecen-ce-ga-srecnega-naredim.html|title=Zame je vsak dan srečen, če ga srečnega naredim|publisher=Delo.si|accessdate=11 November 2017|language=Slovenian}}</ref> Before studying in university she attended general educational course in mathematics and physics under the auspices of the People’s University. One of her professors there was the mathematician, [[Emilija Mlakar Branc]], of whomAleksandra later said that had "initiated her into logical thinking for life".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pivec |first=Franci |date=26 October 2020 |title=V spomin legendarni AKF |trans-title=In memory of the legendary AKF |url=https://blog.cobiss.si/2020/10/26/v-spomin-legendarni-akf/ |accessdate=2026-02-27 |website=Blog COBISS |language=sl}}</ref>

==Career==
Between 1954 and 1980, Frazer carried out extensive research into [[alkaloids]] and [[Antibiotic|antibiotics]] for pharmaceutical companies. After 1980 she combined her chemical research with lecturing and was employed as a researcher for international organizations including the [[EU]], [[UNDP]], [[UNESCO]], [[ILO]], and the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]]. In her later life she was notably involved with promoting clean technologies, and in 1999 she was the first woman scientist to be given the [[Honda Prize]] in [[Tokyo]] for her development of knowledge in this field.<ref name="rtvslo1"/>

In the 1960s and 1970s, she was active in politics, she also held the office of vice president of the Executive Council of Slovenia (during the [[Stane Kavčič]] era<ref>{{cite web|author=Jasna Kontler Salamon |url=https://www.delo.si/sobotna-priloga/vecini-razumnikov-zamerim-da-molcijo-in-ne-opozarjajo-kje-je-nevarnost-142173.html |title=Večini razumnikov zamerim, da molčijo in ne opozarjajo, kje je nevarnost |publisher=Delo.si |date= |accessdate=20 May 2020}}</ref>), where she was in charge of health, culture, science, and education sectors. After three years in office, she returned to academia.<ref name="rtvslo1"/>

Outside her native Slovenia she worked with universities in Switzerland, the UK and the US, and domestically she hosted over 60 international seminars and workshops. Frazer was a member of the United Nations Council, the [[World Academy of Art and Science]] and the [[Academia Europaea]] in London (since 1988)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kornhauser_Aleksandra |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328142618/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kornhauser_Aleksandra |title=Aleksandra Kornhauser |publisher=Academia Europaea |date= |archive-date=28 March 2019}}</ref> and was a recipient of the [[Laurent Lavoisier Medal]] of the [[Académie de Pharmacie]] and the [[Robert Brasted Memorial Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]], among others.<ref name="rtvslo1"/>

She was professionally active until the age of 90, when she concluded her term as the dean of [[Jožef Stefan International Postgraduate School]].<ref name="rtvslo1926">{{cite web|url=https://val202.rtvslo.si/2020/05/aleksandra-kornhauser-frazer-1926-2020/ |title=Aleksandra Kornhauser Frazer (1926–2020) – Val 202 |publisher=Val202.rtvslo.si |date= |accessdate=19 May 2020}}</ref> She received the [[Zois Prize]] for life-time achievements in 1997, the highest prize in the scientific field in Slovenia. She was also an honorary citizen of [[Ljubljana]].

==Personal life==
Frazer was married twice. Her first husband was Pavle Kornhauser, a Slovenian [[physician]]. Her second husband was British chemist, Malcolm Frazer, Professor of a Chemical Education at the [[University of East Anglia]] and subsequently chief executive of the [[Council for National Academic Awards]]. She kept both surnames of her husbands.<ref>
